title: Patience through Him
hook: be patient, and your patience is only through Allah (16:127)
tomorrow: By night, from mosque to mosque

segments.voice: Yesterday, hikmah, wisdom, and your line was argue in the best way. Did you say someone's best point back to them before making yours? How did it land? Day four hundred fifty-six.

You've told yourself to be patient a hundred times. Count to ten. Breathe. Don't send it. And sometimes it works, and sometimes, on the eleventh count, you send it anyway. Patience, it turns out, is hard to manufacture on command. The last verses of An-Nahl know this. They're said, in the commentaries, to come at one of the most painful moments of the Prophet's life, and their answer to it is not try harder. It's something stranger.

Many commentators connect these verses to the battle of Uhud. The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ found the body of his uncle Hamza, killed and mutilated, and in his grief, the reports say, he spoke of repaying it many times over. Verse 126 answers: if you punish, punish only to the measure of the harm done to you. But if you're patient, that is better for the patient. Then verse 127 speaks to him directly. In Pickthall's words: "Thine endurance is only by (the help of) Allah." Sit with that. The verse gives a command, be patient, and in the same breath says you can't do it alone. Sabr, the Arabic word, comes from a root meaning to hold back, to restrain, to keep something in place. Arabic speakers use it for holding yourself steady when everything in you wants to lurch. And the verse says that steadiness is given. It goes on: don't grieve over them, and don't be distressed by their schemes. Then the surah's last line: God is with those who are mindful of Him and those who do good. Muhsinun, people of ihsan, the excellence of verse ninety. A hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari puts the same idea from another side: whoever tries to be patient, God will make them patient, and no one is given a gift better or wider than patience. So patience isn't a muscle you build alone, or only a mood that falls on you. You reach for it, and it's handed to you. That's how An-Nahl ends: the surah of gifts, uncountable favors, milk, honey, wisdom, closes by naming patience as one more of them.
screen: `UHUD, AND HAMZA'S BODY.` · `ONLY TO THE MEASURE OF THE HARM.` · `SABR: TO HOLD STEADY.` · `YOU REACH, AND IT'S GIVEN.` · then, large: `YOUR PATIENCE IS ONLY THROUGH GOD.`

segments.voice: The practice is to ask for patience. Sit, and think of the place in your life where you're running out of it: a person, a wait, a body that isn't healing fast enough. Feel where the impatience sits, maybe in your jaw, or your chest. Breathe there. If you pray, you can ask God for patience with that one thing, in your own words. If you don't, simply notice that you're asking for something you can't produce by force, and let the asking be enough for now. The bell holds the time.
Sabr. Patience, holding steady: commanded and given in the same verse, the last gift named in the surah of the bee. Today's word.
Your line: patience is from him. Today, the moment you feel it running out, stop and ask for more before you answer. Day four hundred fifty-six.

screen: `DAY 456 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: BY NIGHT, FROM MOSQUE TO MOSQUE.`

howItsDone: Muslims speak of sabr as one of the central virtues and often ask God for patience in du'a; 16:126–128 is cited in teaching on restraint, proportion in retaliation and forgiveness.

fork.setup: your uncle has been killed and mutilated, and you're grieving. the verses come. what do they allow you?
options: punish only to the measure of the harm; patience is better.
nothing at all; any response is forbidden.
fork.reveal: 16:126 limits any response to the harm done, then says patience is better, and 16:127 says that patience comes through God.

original.note: Arabic: patience, endurance; from a root meaning to hold back, to keep steady.

trapdoor: what you thought: be patient, try harder.
what it means: patience is commanded and given at once: you reach for it, and God supplies it.
what a scholar hears: 16:126–128 are tied by many commentators to Uhud; the surah closes on the muhsinun, echoing ihsan in 16:90.

sources.quoted: Thine endurance is only by (the help of) Allah.

notes: Pickthall wording of 16:127 ('Thine endurance is only by (the help of) Allah.') quoted from memory; confirm exactly.
The link of 16:126–128 to Uhud and Hamza is one view in tafsir (others place these verses at the conquest of Mecca or treat them generally); confirm framing 'many commentators'.
Bukhari 1469 number cited from memory; confirm.

Audit (y2 second sample): the teach's large screen line showed Pickthall's 16:127 with '(the help of)' silently cut ('THINE ENDURANCE IS ONLY BY ALLAH.'), which presents an altered quotation as the verse; it is now a plain paraphrase, 'YOUR PATIENCE IS ONLY THROUGH GOD.', matching the match game.
